description:
Scenario: A future test author copies the pattern of set_create_uniqueness_violation_returns_already_exists (metadata.rs:692) which calls backend.force_create_error(...) then does ONE create. The next test in the file gets a fresh backend (test functions own their MockBackend), so the stickiness doesn't bite. But if a test author chains operations on the same MockBackend instance, the stickiness silently affects every subsequent create_object call.

clear_forced_create_error at lib.rs:222 is annotated #[allow(dead_code)] — the codebase tells the compiler 'never used, suppress warning'. This is a maintenance smell: the cleanup helper exists but is dead. Either it should be used by some test (revealing that stickiness was a problem worth managing), or it should be deleted (with the documented sticky behavior or remove it from MockBackend).

Maintenance consequence:
(a) Future test author writes 'create one, see uniqueness error, then create a different object expecting success' — fails because forced_create_error is still set.
(b) The dead_code allow hides the warning, so the dead helper goes unnoticed.

Fix direction: either:
(i) Remove force_create_error's stickiness — auto-reset after one use. Update existing tests if needed.
(ii) Have at least one existing test exercise clear_forced_create_error, removing the dead_code allow.
(iii) Remove force_create_error entirely and force tests to inject errors via a different mechanism (e.g. parameterized MockBackend with a closure).
title: test_support::MockBackend.force_create_error is sticky, never resets after a test uses it — clear_forced_create_error is dead code (annotated #[allow(dead_code)])
